items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: Jonah Jones was in there with Cozy Cole, that bunch.

ctx.x: excellent tape recorded interview with you a short, called Swing Street.
Right. And since Frankie Newton had been down in the area, there was a group that was playing opposite Stuff, that Spirits of the Rhythm.
And then before theat, there was -- Jonah Jones was in there with Cozy Cole, that bunch.

items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: Claude Thornhill brought her in, heard her in Pittsburgh and recommended her.

ctx.x: So, Saturday come and so they called up -- somebody calls up from New York, long distance on the phone, and says, "We want to speak to Stuff Smith." So Stuff says okay, so he answered the phone. So he come back to the bandstand and I said who was that. He said some guy said he was Bern Back. And Bern Back was a big man, official, in the national union, not 802, in the national. Bern Back was his name. So he said it was some guy said it was Bern Back, said not to leave. He said, "Stay on your job." So we said we…

So that morning, we got on the train and we come on back home. And we laid around awhile. So Joe Helbarth had been telling us come on back, because they wasn't doing too good in there, you know. Business was bad, because Kirby hadn't got the band set. In fact I don't know if it was Kirby's band or not, because they had Leo Watson they were trying to take out of the Spirits of Rhythm. They took Leo out of there, and they had Pete Brown. They had Frankie Newton and some other guys. So maybe he had -- yeah, he did,…
Scottish songs, they had brought the band up with her, you see.
